title: add RAG agent quickstarts and tool-calling examples; docs site updates
author: Alex Kim
release_notes: Added RAG agent quickstarts and several tool-calling example notebooks; docs site sidebar updated to include new quickstarts. No breaking changes.
description:
Context: Add a set of RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) agent quickstarts and tool-calling examples to help engineers onboard to Redwood's agent patterns and the recommended tool interface. Motivation: several customers and internal teams requested canonical quickstarts that demonstrate (1) a RAG agent wired to a document store + vector search, (2) tool-calling patterns for safe external actions, and (3) structured output validation for QA and monitoring. This PR bundles docs + runnable examples + docs-site navigation updates.

Summary of changes (high level): - New quickstart guide: docs/quickstarts/rag-agent.md that walks through architecture, config, and step-by-step code. - Two runnable examples under examples/rag-agent/: a Python notebook (rag_agent_quickstart.ipynb) and a lightweight TS example (rag-agent-tool-calling.ts) demonstrating tool invocation and structured responses. - Example vector-store glue code using Redis/FAISS adapter (examples/rag-agent/adapters). - Updated docs site sidebar and landing page to surface the quickstarts (website/sidebars.js, website/docs/index.md). - Small improvements to the agents API reference to call out the tool-calling schema and validation examples.

Checklist: - [x] Quickstart draft with runnable snippets - [x] Python and TS examples included and smoke-tested locally - [x] Docs site sidebar updated - [x] CI docs build passes - [x] Reviewed by docs and platform engineers

Why this change: Standardizing on a short, reproducible RAG + agent quickstart reduces onboarding time for new users and provides a canonical example for internal feature work (routing, caching, and safety checks). The tool-calling examples show recommended request/response shapes and a safe executor pattern.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on accuracy of the code samples, clarity of the step-by-step setup (credentials, vector store selection), and the API reference addition for the tool-calling schema. The examples intentionally keep external dependencies minimal and mock network calls where possible to avoid flakiness in CI.
